name: a dollar-quoted body is one statement, as it always was
sql:
CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS int AS $fn$ BEGIN RETURN 1; END; $fn$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
SELECT f();

statements.sql: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS int AS $fn$ BEGIN RETURN 1; END; $fn$ LANGUAGE plpgsql

name: a function written in SQL keeps its BEGIN ATOMIC body

statements.sql:
CREATE FUNCTION add_one(n int) RETURNS int
LANGUAGE sql
BEGIN ATOMIC
  SELECT n + 1;
END

name: a CASE inside a BEGIN ATOMIC body ends nothing
sql: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE p() LANGUAGE sql BEGIN ATOMIC SELECT CASE WHEN true THEN 1 END; END; CALL p()

statements.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE p() LANGUAGE sql BEGIN ATOMIC SELECT CASE WHEN true THEN 1 END; END

name: BEGIN on its own is a transaction, not a body
a semicolon inside parentheses ends nothing, as psql reads it
sql:
CREATE RULE r AS ON INSERT TO t DO ALSO (INSERT INTO a VALUES (1); INSERT INTO b VALUES (2));
SELECT 1

statements.sql: CREATE RULE r AS ON INSERT TO t DO ALSO (INSERT INTO a VALUES (1); INSERT INTO b VALUES (2))

a trigger whose body is one IF

INSERT INTO x VALUES (1);

statements.sql: CREATE TRIGGER t BEFORE INSERT ON x FOR EACH ROW IF NEW.a < 0 THEN SET NEW.a = 0; END IF

the function IF and DDL's IF EXISTS open no block

name: a CASE outside a body opens no block, so a typo in one swallows nothing

SELECT CASE WHEN a THEN 1 FROM t;

sql:
CREATE TEMP TRIGGER t AFTER INSERT ON n WHEN CASE WHEN NEW.id > 0 THEN 1 END BEGIN SELECT 1; END;
SELECT 2

name: BEGIN on its own is a transaction
GO ends a batch, and a procedure runs to it
GO n runs its batch n times
IF … ; ELSE … is one statement
sql:
IF 1 = 1 SELECT 1; ELSE SELECT 2;
SELECT 3;

name: BEGIN TRAN is a statement, not a block

statements.sql: UPDATE t SET a = 1 WHERE id = 1

name: TRY and CATCH are blocks
a body with no BEGIN runs to the end of its batch

statements.sql: CREATE PROCEDURE p AS SET NOCOUNT ON; SELECT 1

name: a ; after a procedure's BEGIN … END ends it
sql:
CREATE PROCEDURE p AS BEGIN SELECT 1; END;
EXEC p;

statements.sql: CREATE PROCEDURE p AS BEGIN SELECT 1; END

name: END CONVERSATION ends no block
GO in a text or a comment separates nothing
go in any case, with a comment after it
sql:
SELECT 1
go -- next batch
SELECT 2

name: a CASE outside a block opens nothing; inside one its END is its own

statements.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN 1 = 1 THEN 1 FROM t
BEGIN SELECT CASE WHEN 1 = 1 THEN 1 END; END

name: a PL/SQL block runs to its / and keeps its last semicolon
CREATE PROCEDURE is PL/SQL, and / ends a plain statement too
a PL/SQL block with no / runs to the end of the text
a / after a statement that ended is no second run of it
sql:
SELECT 1 FROM dual;
/
SELECT 2 FROM dual
/

name: a package and its body
a query that declares a function is PL/SQL

statements.sql:
WITH FUNCTION twice(n NUMBER) RETURN NUMBER IS BEGIN RETURN n * 2; END;
SELECT twice(2) FROM dual
